summary:
**EARTHSONIC – Hear the Planet Change** is an interactive web-based sonification platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the challenge of making Earth science visualizations more accessible, particularly for people who are blind or visually impaired.

We developed a platform that transforms NASA Earth visualization frames into real-time audio across four records: Night Lights, Lightning from the ISS, GEOS Aerosols, and Ocean Currents. Using image processing and HTML Canvas, the application analyzes visual features such as brightness, color, spatial distribution, pixel density, and changes between consecutive frames. These features are mapped to musical properties, including pitch, rhythm, timbre, and stereo position, with Tone.js generating the audio dynamically.

EARTHSONIC also includes audio descriptions, keyboard navigation, high-contrast mode, reduced-motion controls, and an interactive explanation panel. By turning visual patterns into sound, our project offers an alternative way to explore and experience our changing planet, promoting accessibility, scientific engagement, and inclusive interaction with Earth science.
details:
EARTHSONIC – Hear the Planet Change

EARTHSONIC is an interactive web-based sonification platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It transforms NASA Earth visualization videos into sound, allowing users to experience changes in our planet through audio rather than relying only on visual information. The project particularly aims to make Earth science more accessible to people who are blind or visually impaired.

How It Works

The platform uses four NASA Earth visualization records: Night Lights, Lightning from the ISS, GEOS Aerosols, and Ocean Currents. We downloaded the visualization videos and used FFmpeg to extract image frames. These frames are processed using HTML Canvas and reduced to a 64 × 36 grid for visual analysis.

The application analyzes visual characteristics such as brightness, colour, spatial position, pixel density, and changes between consecutive frames. These features are mapped to musical properties:

  • Brightness → Pitch: Brighter regions produce higher notes.
  • Colour → Timbre: Visual colour characteristics influence the sound texture.
  • Horizontal position → Stereo pan: Sounds are positioned across the left and right audio channels.
  • Pixel density → Note density: More visual activity can produce denser musical patterns.
  • Frame-to-frame changes → Audio intensity: Changes influence the dynamics and intensity of the sound.
  • Sudden bright flashes → Percussion: Rapid visual events can trigger percussive sounds.

Tone.js generates the audio in real time, creating an interactive experience in which users can listen to different Earth visualizations and explore how their visual patterns translate into sound.

Benefits and Intended Impact

EARTHSONIC provides an alternative way to explore Earth science information without depending entirely on visual interpretation. It aims to:

  • Improve accessibility for blind and visually impaired users.
  • Make complex Earth science visualizations more engaging and easier to explore.
  • Encourage auditory learning and multisensory interaction.
  • Help users notice spatial patterns and changes in Earth's systems through sound.
  • Promote inclusive access to scientific information and environmental awareness.

Tools and Technologies Used

  • Frontend: React.js, TypeScript, HTML5, CSS3
  • Audio generation: Tone.js and Web Audio API
  • Visual processing: HTML Canvas and JavaScript
  • Video processing: FFmpeg for extracting frames from NASA visualization videos
  • Development tools: Visual Studio Code, Git and GitHub
  • AI assistance: ChatGPT and Claude for code generation, debugging, technical guidance, and documentation.

The project was developed using a standard computer and browser-based technologies. No specialized hardware was required.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of EARTHSONIC lies in translating scientific visual information into an auditory experience. Instead of simply displaying NASA visualizations, the platform allows users to listen to patterns, movement, intensity, and changes represented in those visualizations.

Each record has a different visual character and therefore creates a different sound experience. This combines image processing, sound synthesis, interactive web development, and accessibility-focused design in one platform.

Factors Considered During Development

Our team considered accessibility, usability, scientific context, performance, and reliability throughout development. We aimed to make the interface easy to navigate while ensuring that the audio mappings were understandable and meaningful. We also considered browser performance when processing video frames, clear controls for interacting with the audio, and the importance of crediting NASA as the source of the visualizations.

EARTHSONIC is designed as an accessible and creative bridge between Earth science and sound, helping more people experience and connect with the changing planet.

NASA visualization credit: NASA Earth Information Center / Scientific Visualization Studio. This project is an independent student project and is not endorsed by NASA.
